title: Will the Trump administration or a GOP state governor deploy armed officers or troops to a polling or early voting site in 2026?
resolution_criteria:
This question resolves as **Yes** if active duty United States military personnel, National Guard members, federal officers, or state troopers are deployed by the U.S. federal government or a Republican state governor to any polling or early-voting site, while that site is open for in-person voting for the [2026 general elections](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2026_United_States_elections).

In order to count, the personnel or troops must be armed with firearms and must be either inside the voting site or within 250 feet of its entrance.
fine_print:
For purposes of this question, deliberate deployment for any stated reason counts regardless of stated purpose (e.g., ICE officers enforcing immigration laws or National Guard with the stated purpose of protecting voters).

State troopers are defined as law enforcement officers working for state-level law enforcement agencies. Officers of sub-state level agencies such as county sheriff’s departments or municipal police departments do not count.

A deployment by a Republican state governor counts if it is ordered by the governor or, in cases where the deployment order is issued by another state official, when it is specifically authorized by the governor. 

Personnel present in a personal capacity (such as voting or serving as poll workers) do not count.

Personnel whose physical closeness to a polling location is incidental to their other duties, including personnel passing through an area, would not count, as long as their presence is coincidental and unrelated to that site or there is a lack of uncontroversial credible reporting that they were deliberately deployed there.

This question will resolve based upon reporting from [credible sources](https://www.metaculus.com/faq/#definitions).

Locations used solely as drop boxes for mail-in or absentee ballots do not count.
